title: The Reformed differ on how grace moves the will
source_text: L. Porro quamvis Scholae Reformatae Doctores in eo conveniant gratiam non tantum in hominis mentem, sed etiam in voluntatem efficaciam suam exerere, eamque potenter & infallibiliter ad bonum flectere & determinare: inter eos tamen est aliquis dissensus de modo quo gratia voluntatem nostram movet, ut in Deum feratur, & bono consentiat.
pass_a_gloss: L. Further, although the Doctors of the Reformed School agree in this, that grace exerts its efficacy not only on the mind of man, but also on the will, and bends & determines it powerfully & infallibly to good: yet among them there is some disagreement about the manner in which grace moves our will, so that it may be carried toward God, & consent to the good.
pass_b_english: Thesis L. Further, the teachers of the Reformed school all agree that grace exerts its efficacy not just on the human mind but on the will as well, and that it bends and settles the will toward the good with power and without fail.
Where they part company is over how grace moves our will so that it turns toward God and gives its assent to what is good.
